clue.text: Illness caused by grouse

definitions.meaning: an ailment or disorder of the body
as a noun, a grumble or moan

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a medical disorder and an expressed grievance, two unrelated senses.

clue.text: Pace had famous sportsman perhaps bowled out

indicators.note: out signals that the bowled letter is dropped from the famous person

parts.note: a well-known sports star is one example of a celebrity
B is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for bowled

explanation.surface: A star player's speed counted for little once he was bowled out at cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowled out' reads as cricket, but 'out' removes B (bowled) from CELEBRITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Celerity is a formal synonym for swiftness or speed.

clue.text: Dam in China river

parts.note: rhyming slang: china plate = mate

explanation.surface: A reservoir wall stands across a river in China.
explanation.walkthrough: China is Cockney rhyming slang: 'china plate' rhymes with mate, meaning friend. Dam is a mother, usually of an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A dam is an animal's mother, and the Latin-derived word is schoolboy slang for mother.

clue.text: Least suitable trench in which to build a stand

definitions.text: in which to build a stand
definitions.note: describes the kind of final defensive position, used adjectivally

parts.note: the last person for a job is the least suitable one
a ditch is a dug trench

explanation.surface: Soldiers pick the worst possible trench to dig in for a defence.
explanation.walkthrough: A last-ditch stand is a final desperate defence, made in the last trench before defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: A final desperate defence is called a last-ditch stand, so the phrase describes where such resistance is made.

clue.text: Island motorway, out of date, causing standstill

parts.note: M is a British motorway, as in the M1
passé means old-fashioned

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned motorway on an island leads to traffic jams.
explanation.walkthrough: British motorways are numbered with M, as in the M25.
explanation.definitionFit: An impasse is a deadlock, a situation where no progress is possible.

clue.text: Chap got up in new suit can be a crashing bore

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other
new signals the letters of suit are made over into a fresh order
in a down clue, got up means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A man dressed in a new suit turns out to be a dreadful bore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got up' turns MAN into NAM, which goes 'in' TSUI, the anagram of SUIT signalled by 'new'. A bore is also a tidal wave in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A tidal bore is a wave surging up a river, so a giant crashing wave is a crashing bore.

clue.text: Source of Doyle's Study in Fear

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it starts, its first letter

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it

explanation.surface: A Sherlock Holmes title, 'A Study in Scarlet', is twisted into a study in fear.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes Conan Doyle's first Holmes novel, A Study in Scarlet.
explanation.definitionFit: Dread is a strong synonym for fear or terror.

clue.text: Submit to delay

explanation.definitionFit: One verb means both to yield to another's authority and to postpone an action.

clue.text: Kick out menial attempting to become equal

indicators.note: a kick sends these letters flying into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A servant is thrown out for trying to rise to his master's level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kick out' reads as dismissal, but only 'Kick' is the anagram signal; OUT is part of the letters with MENIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Emulation is the effort to match or equal another person, a close synonym of imitation.

clue.text: Confounded race journalist!

parts.note: a dash is a sprint
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: An exclamation at a reporter rushing about.
explanation.definitionFit: Dashed and confounded are both mild old-fashioned oaths meaning damned.

clue.text: Fruit that sent many round the bend

definitions.text: Fruit that sent many round the bend

parts.words: Fruit that sent many round the bend
parts.note: in Homer, a fruit eaten by Odysseus's men made them forget home and lose their wits

explanation.definitionFit: Lotus-eaters in the Odyssey ate a fruit that left them dreamy and indifferent.

clue.text: Bags extra boundaries

parts.note: plus means in addition
in cricket a boundary along the ground scores four runs

explanation.surface: A batsman gets extra boundaries in bulk.
explanation.walkthrough: Bags is slang for loose trousers; a ball hit along the ground to the boundary scores four runs in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Bags is old slang for baggy trousers, and these are wide knickerbockers worn by golfers.

clue.text: Church screen was about twice the same size originally

indicators.note: twice means the piece is used two times

parts.note: re means concerning
do., short for ditto, means the same

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A church screen was once about double its present size.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' gives RE, doubled by 'twice'; DO is ditto; 'originally' takes the S of size. 'was' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A reredos is an ornamental screen or panel behind a church altar.

clue.text: What you pay to get this up on a plastic tray

definitions.text: What you pay to get this up on a plastic tray

parts.words: What you pay to get this up on a plastic tray
parts.note: the price of a flight, punning on fare as the food served aloft on a tray

explanation.definitionFit: The ticket price for flying is named from the air plus fare, which also means food served.

clue.text: Grasp the cracker to produce a big surprise

parts.note: to grasp is to take
taken as written
a cracker is a dry biscuit

explanation.surface: Seizing a cracker causes a shock.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something so outrageous it surpasses everything, a startling surprise.

clue.text: Feed English king disguised in position of great danger

indicators.note: disguised means these letters appear in altered form

explanation.surface: Feeding a king in disguise is a risky business.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on a knife-edge means being in a precarious, dangerous balance.

clue.text: You won't get a good deal out of one character that's not natural

definitions.text: You won't get a good deal out of one

parts.note: a card is an eccentric or amusing person
in music a sharp note is not natural

explanation.surface: Someone shady and peculiar will never give you a fair bargain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deal' refers to dealing cards; in music a note is natural, sharp or flat.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheat at card games deals dishonestly, so a fair hand is never on offer.

clue.text: Climber needs a sound transmitter

indicators.note: sound means the word is spoken and heard, giving a soundalike spelling

parts.note: a sender transmits a message

explanation.surface: A mountaineer requires a good radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like an adjective (a sound transmitter), but it signals SENDER said aloud, spelt SCENDER.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascender is one who climbs, and also a climbing device or letter stroke rising up.

clue.text: In the absence of horses, this is unrestricted

definitions.meaning: a string is a trainer's stable of racehorses, so lacking such strings

explanation.definitionFit: An offer with no strings attached has no conditions, while strings of racehorses supply the literal pun.

clue.text: In court drunk, and in a nervy state

parts.note: to be up before a judge is to be in court
tight is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: A drunk in court is understandably anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: Uptight is informal for tense, anxious and on edge.

clue.text: Relative makes his way over

parts.note: steps means walks or makes progress
on means on top of, over

explanation.surface: A family member travels across.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepson is a relation by marriage, a spouse's son.

clue.text: Discharges radio operator.

definitions.meaning: electrical flashes, or the verb throws off fiery particles
nickname for a ship's wireless operator

explanation.definitionFit: The word means electrical discharges and is the traditional nickname of a ship's wireless operator.

clue.text: An old overseas entertainer

parts.note: a white-faced clown from the old seaside pier shows, performing on a pier over the sea

explanation.definitionFit: A pierrot was a seaside clown who performed in troupes on piers built out over the sea.

clue.text: Not fully, reliable, being out of practice

indicators.note: not fully means a piece of the word is missing, here its first letter

parts.note: trusty means dependable

explanation.surface: Not entirely dependable after a long lay-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not fully' removes the first letter T from TRUSTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Rusty skills have deteriorated through lack of use.

clue.text: The heart of a city church

parts.note: Essen is a German city
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: At the centre of a city stands its church.
explanation.walkthrough: Essen is a city in Germany's Ruhr; CE is the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: The essence of something is its core or heart.

clue.text: Order only new fabric

indicators.note: order means the letters are put into a new sequence

explanation.surface: An instruction to buy only new cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylon is a synthetic fabric.

clue.text: Makes new, arrangement of coloured flags without using first pole

parts.note: red is a colour

indicators.note: the first instance of the pole letter in flags is left out

parts.note: ensigns are flags
N is a pole, the North Pole

explanation.surface: A designer reorders a display of coloured flags without the first pole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without using first' drops the first N of ENSIGNS, leaving ESIGNS; 'arrangement of' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: To redesign is to make something afresh to a new plan.

clue.text: Girl's back was giving trouble

indicators.note: back means the name is read from the end

parts.note: Delia is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl's back was hurting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reads like her spine but turns DELIA round.
explanation.definitionFit: Ailed means troubled or was unwell.

clue.text: Unseemly compact disc is broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast signals the letters said out loud

parts.note: CD is a compact disc

explanation.surface: An indecent disc gets airplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Seedy means sordid or disreputable.

clue.text: Can batsman take off cap, having secured this?

definitions.text: Can batsman take off cap, having secured this?

parts.note: a tin is a can
an opener is a batsman who starts the innings

explanation.surface: A cricketer wonders whether he can doff his cap after securing a win.
explanation.walkthrough: An opener starts the batting in cricket; the device takes the lid off a tin.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue asks whether, having obtained such a tool, one can remove a tin's lid.
